text_plugin_synopsis: Runs JavaScript with an independent QuickJS engine in an isolated Android process
p_languages_all_supported: The current README.md supports the following languages
p_introduction: QuickJS Runtime is a standalone Android plugin that lets AutoJs6 select [QuickJS]({{ quickjs_official_url }}) as an independent JavaScript engine. Every request gets a fresh native runtime and context inside the isolated `:quickjs_runtime` process. Source and events cross a versioned Binder contract, so this is real QuickJS execution and not an alias for Rhino, Node.js, or Bun.
usage_steps: Use AutoJs6 build {{ required_host_version_code }} ({{ required_host_version_name }}) or later on Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) or later.
Install the release APK matching the device ABI, or use the larger `universal` APK when the ABI is unknown.
Open the AutoJs6 plugin center and enable QuickJS Runtime. If Android left the newly installed package stopped, use the host `Activate` action.

Select QuickJS with the standalone `"quickjs";` directive at the beginning of a `.js` or `.mjs` file, or name the file `*.quickjs.js` for script mode or `*.quickjs.mjs` for ES module mode; then run it normally from AutoJs6.
p_usage_note: Version 1.0 accepts one immutable source snapshot per request. It does not transfer a project tree or resolve relative file imports, and it deliberately exposes no AutoJs6 globals, Java bridge, filesystem, network, `std`, or `os` module.
p_quick_start_intro: Run this file to confirm that AutoJs6 selected QuickJS and started the native runtime
p_quick_start_result: The output identifies QuickJS {{ quickjs_version }}, prints Unicode text, and evaluates a BigInt expression.
compatibility_points: Engine: official QuickJS {{ quickjs_version }}, revision `{{ quickjs_revision }}`, commit [`{{ quickjs_commit }}`]({{ quickjs_commit_url }}), with source archive SHA-256 `{{ quickjs_archive_sha256 }}`.
Platform: Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) or later. Single-ABI APKs support `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, `x86_64`, and `x86`; the `universal` APK contains all four.
Language: JavaScript scripts and single-file ES modules are supported, including BigInt, Unicode, Promise jobs, and module top-level await. TypeScript is not parsed.

Request bounds: source up to {{ max_source_size }}, combined stdout and stderr up to {{ max_output_size }}, default timeout {{ default_timeout }}, default memory {{ default_memory_limit }}, maximum memory {{ maximum_memory_limit }}, and default stack {{ default_stack_limit }}.

Runtime boundary: only bounded `console` and `print` output helpers are added by the plugin. Host automation APIs, Java objects, filesystem and network APIs, `std`, `os`, native addons, timers, and multi-file module graphs are outside version 1.0.
security_points: The Wake activity and both exported services require `org.autojs.permission.PLUGIN`; execution occurs under the plugin UID in the separate `:quickjs_runtime` process.
Each request receives a new `JSRuntime` and `JSContext`. Memory, stack, time, source, and output limits are enforced, and cancellation reaches the QuickJS interrupt handler.
Source arrives through a read-only `ParcelFileDescriptor`. Output uses bounded oneway callback chunks, while terminal Bundles contain only status and diagnostic summaries.

The repository vendors byte-exact files from the pinned official archive and verifies sizes and SHA-256 digests. `quickjs-libc`, filesystem helpers, and network helpers are not compiled into the engine.
p_plugin_interface: Stable identifiers and limits for AutoJs6 host and plugin developers
p_contract: `QuickJsRuntimeService` is discovered by action `{{ plugin_service_action }}` and category `{{ plugin_service_category }}`. `runScript` receives a request Bundle and a read-only source descriptor, streams bounded stdout and stderr events through the callback, and returns a terminal Bundle containing status, timing, and diagnostics. `cancelScript` is safe before or during dispatch, and `prewarmRuntime` performs a native engine readiness check.
p_16kb_status: 16 KB status: the native linker is configured for 16 KB maximum page size, and the APK verifier checks each ELF PT_LOAD alignment plus uncompressed ZIP data alignment. End-to-end execution was validated on an API 37 x86_64 `google_apis_ps16k` emulator reporting `PAGE_SIZE=16384`; all three Binder and QuickJS instrumentation suites passed.
p_build_intro: Building requires JDK 17 or later, Python 3, Android SDK 36, NDK 28.2.13676358, and CMake 3.22.1. The standard checks verify the pinned QuickJS source, generated documentation, JVM tests, all APK variants, instrumentation packaging, Android Lint, ELF alignment, and native-library inventory.
p_localization: Edit the JSON and Markdown templates, then run `py .python/generate_markdown.py`. Generated README, changelog, and plugin-instruction files must not be edited by hand. The `--check` mode validates language shape, version alignment, localized resources, orphan files, and generated-file drift without writing.

p_instruction_backend: This release embeds the pinned official QuickJS {{ quickjs_version }} source as a native library and creates a fresh runtime for every request. Source is read from an immutable descriptor; stdout, stderr, errors, cancellation, limits, and completion return through the host contract.
p_instruction_more: See the [project README]({{ repo_url }}) for ABI selection, exact limits, security properties, build verification, and the complete version 1.0 scope.
